Q: Modular monolith vs microservices for ERP system with multiple business modules A:

Is this meant to be a multi-tenant SaaS app? Or something a client could host themselves? (avoid complexity if on-prem). If SaaS and multi-tenant, any idea of user count and planned growth rate? And what would multi-tenant look like? row level tenant ownership, or db per client or schema per client? For shared user information - an auth cookie could carry that - that is basically how Ory identity stack manages it. For other data - does it all have to be one big DB? Microservices do make sense as you scale - for example, you can move observability to their own nodes, or identity to different nodes, as loads get larger.

Q: Custom 32-bit OS: Protected Mode GUI (VGA Mode 13h) hangs with black screen, although console works A:

Your project grew

... and you forgot to modify some of your early assumptions!

mov al, 8; 8 sectors for stage2 (2KB)

See this comment that still talks about 2KB, whereas the instruction wants to load 8 sectors which equals 4KB.

call set_video_mode_bios

Besides setting the video mode, this routine also stores some variables at address 0x5000 and onward. These will all get destroyed by the loading of the kernel at 0x2000.

mov di, 0x2000 ; Temporary buffer
call load_kernel
;  Copy kernel to 0x1000 (entry point via link.ld)
call copy_kernel

You load the kernel at this temporary address to stay away from your running stage 2, that's fine (although the stack that sits below 0x7C00 gets it full in the face!), but the subsequent copy_kernel overwrites the very code that is doing the copying! (And via the call it corrupts the freshly loaded kernel.) It also overwrites the code that should setup the protected mode; How does your emulator not show you that you don't reach protected mode?

 mov cx, 0xC800 ; 100 sectors * 512 / 2 (words)

You copy way too much! The rep movsw is going to copy 51200 words, because although your comment mentions / 2 (words), the instruction was not changed accordingly.

load_kernel:
; We read 128 sectors starting from sector 3 (after boot + stage2)
; boot = sector 1, stage2 = sectors 2-3, kernel = from sector 4
...
mov al, 100 ; 100 sectors = 50KB (should be enough for the kernel)
mov cl, 10 ; starting at sector 10
mov dl, 0x00 ; floppy disk 0

Be precise:
You state to read 128 sectors, but actually ask for 100.
You state stage 2 occupies 2 sectors, but it actually occupies 8 sectors.
You state from sector 4, but actually ask from sector 10.

Are you sure that your kernel resides on a floppy disk? You'd better use the same DL that BIOS gave you at the start of stage 1.
Further, to avoid disk/dma troubles it is better to repeat 100 times loading a single sector, than trying to load 100 sectors at once.

In short, your 'video problem' starts much earlier than the switch to the protected mode...

Q: Animating launch screen zoom A:

You cannot animate your LaunchScreen. Most of the apps in which you see animation actually have an intermediate controller/screen. Flow would be some thing like this.

  1. Launch Screen (You can't do any thing here. OS will setup your application)
  2. AnimationViewController (This is where you will do some of you initial setup and also animation)
  3. HomeViewController (Rest of the flow for your application).

Q: API in Python, or any other programming language A:

In general, no.

The modem's unique identifier will only be accessible to the the cellular service provider. Any connection beyond that service provider will be made using an IP address signed by the service provider.

The only way for the merchant to get information about their hardware being connected to the Internet without the cooporation of that service provider would be to modify the product they sell so it notifies them.

This would raise red flags (attracting bad press) from privacy advocacy groups.
